text_fidelity_a: OCOOPA Rechargeable Hand Warmers, 10000mAH Electric Handwarmer Winter Warm 15 Hours Portable Hands Heater for Men Women When I was a kid my dad used to hand me his hand warmer when we were outside during cold weather.  It was a "manual" kind - the interior had something like rock wool that was soaked in butane and lit and then the metal casing was slid inside a thick insulated bag and put in your pocket.  It could get rather hot!  I mention this because it brings back fond memories, but also to illustrate the difference in the "old fashioned" hand warmers and this one.  I love how easy this is to charge, even in my car, and the 3 levels of warmth depending on how cold it is and/or what you are doing.  I can put this in my pocket on low heat while I'm scraping the ice off my windshield and windows, then grab the warmer and let my fingers regain some feeling before trading the scraper for the shovel and shoveling the snow away from the car and off the sidewalk.  However many times I need to, I can stop shoveling and grab the warmer to keep my hands and fingers from going numb - that's what I appreciate having this handwarmer!  If you have kids that wait at the bus stop or have to walk to school even in winter, giving them a handwarmer might be just the thing to give them a "boost" of warmth while standing in the cold!

text_fidelity_a:
Wilson Ultra Men's Right-Hand Golf Package Set Includes Irons, Woods, a Putter and a Stand Bag OK, first let me say that I am a beginner golfer (male, 5'11" and 210lb. ) and to clear up some other questions from previous posts, this is what is included:

1-Wood (Driver)
4-Hybrid
FW-Fairway Wood
5,6,7,8,9-Irons
PW-Pitching Wedge
Putter

Now for the review.

At the moment my favorite clubs in this set is the putter, PW, 5-iron and FW. Maybe those are my favorite because I have the most consistent results with them. Now to the point, the FW is the most forgiving wood I have ever used. The Putter, well I loved it the moment I was able to use it on the green... I look forward to getting to the green just so I can pull this baby out. Love the way it taps and it balances GREAT!!! This is not your typical putter. You will love the way it feels when it hits the ball. Trust me on this one. The PW performs very well. When I'm not using my 5-iron I go straight for the Pitching Wedge (but that could be that I am still learning how to position myself for the other irons).

The bag the clubs came in are already setting up the standards for what my future bag should have. The Driver, 4H and FW all had covers for them. The bag has a towel ring and plenty of storage space. I like the tee holster on the side of the bag as well as it is convenient. Additionally, the Bag Stand is activated when you tilt the bag forward...Very Nice...

I can see myself using this set of clubs for a good while. Today I played on the course with 3 of my buddies and all of them have been playing for years and have commented on how much better I am playing with these clubs than the rental sets. And for the price I paid for it I don't think I could have done better. I am happy with this set of clubs and its making my golf learning experience all the more enjoyable.

Thanks to Wilson for manufacturing such a great beginner (to intermediate maybe) set of clubs. The image is accurate for this set of clubs, but unfortunately they don't show all the clubs in the set. But you can Google another site for these same exact clubs and they have more images that you can check out.

Kudos to Amazon for shipping the product fast. I only requested standard delivery and my clubs arrived the next day!!! But that could be since it was shipped out of Pennsylvania to Washington DC. So its not that far away. It was shipped in the original Wilson box. Everything in the package was wrapped and protected during shipment.

John
text_fidelity_b: Wilson Ultra Men's Right-Hand Golf Package Set Includes Irons, Woods, a Putter and a Stand Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs I have other Mazama water bladders, and really wanted to like this. I bought it for a trip to the national parks in UT where you should be carrying more water. The good is that its a big reservoir, and the hose is thicker so the rate of flow is higher than their other hoses. What I love about Mazama is the magnetic holder for the hose, and this one is even better because there is some play in it where as the normal version can pop off at times (I generally wear it while mountain biking and its fine, but if there isn't enough slack in the hose it will pop off the magnet).

What I don't like about this one...the closure for the bladder is not secure. I found out by dumping about two liters of water over me when it was in my backpack and I bent forward. I know it looks like it should work, but because its plastic and malleable there is play there and its not perfect. The "lock" wiggles even without pressure, so its suspect to begin with. The way it opens is nice for cleaning, drying, and filling, and the "spine" is helpful for carrying and moving it around. These features cannot make up for the closure however, and I worry about it whenever the bladder is full. I'm also not a fan of the way the bite valve works...it can be left full open and water will just run out, or you can get it to work if you bite a little...but just a little because if you bit too much the rubber tip falls off. Squirely bugger.

When using in the future I might add a clamp or something to ensure the closure can't slip off, and will use my other hose vs this one.
text_fidelity_b: Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs

This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

Silky YOKI Professional Machette 270mm Chopper (570-27) I spend a lot of time cutting back invasive vegetation in the wetlands surrounding our Southwest Florida home. The Brazilian Pepper tree is a non native plant brought into Florida in the mid-1800's for use as an ornamental plant. Their bright red berries and brilliant green foliage are used frequently as Christmas decorations. However this tree is a member of the same family as poison ivy and can cause reactions to those with sensitive skin as well as respiratory problems for some people when the tree is blooming. These trees can grow up to 10 feet per year and their root systems and canopies expand so quickly that they rob the surrounding vegetation of both water and sunlight. They currently dominate about 700,000 acres of land in Florida.

They also sprout limbs vertically and horizontally and create a very thick network of branches. I have often used a reciprocating saw (with green wood blade) and my Esee Lite Machete to attack the outside perimeter of these trees. But since the areas closest to the trunks are very tight, I couldn't get a full swing on my machete and had to look for a "chopper", something that this Silky Yoki excels at. I have several Silky saws (including folding saws and a pole saw) that are built better and last longer than just about any other saw that I've tried. So I thought that an investment in this chopper was a pretty safe bet.

Machetes are designed for slashing with a full swing. Choppers are, well, made for short and abrupt (primarily) down strokes. Think about a butcher cutting up a side of beef. The weight is concentrated on a shorter blade and of course the blade itself has to be razor sharp. You should be able to achieve the same results with a chopper in a tight space with about the same effort that you'd use with a longer machete in a more open space. And I'm happy to report that the Silky Yoki Chopper performs as well as I expected it to.

The grip is very comfortable, the blade holds an edge all day, and the brush hook on the end helps draw vegetation towards you for disposal. It comes with a hole in the blade for hanging and also a carrying case that matches. The blade is easily touched up with a butcher's steel as long as you follow the natural line and don't get too aggressive. Even if you do abuse the blade, replacements are available. This is a good tool to take with you when hiking, hunting, camping, or clearing brush. It would also make a pretty good defensive tool if you find yourself in a bad situation.
text_fidelity_b: Silky YOKI Professional Machette 270mm Chopper (570-27)

text_fidelity_a:
Birchwood Casey Shoot-N-C, 8" Targets, Adhesive, See Hits Instantly At the time I bought this 30 pack the price was $20 delivered for a per-target price of $0.66 each. This is a great value, as the local Wal-Mart sells a pack that is about $1 each.

Each target is a peel-and-stick "label". It adheres excellent to cardboard and clean, flat surfaces. I adheres OK to rougher surfaces like old, splintering plywood. I affixed this directly to an old shot-up apple crate and ended up having to supplement a little duct tape to keep it on when the wind kicked up.

Every target has four "pasties" that you can peel off and affix to the target after you've shot it. Each pasty is large enough to cover 2 or 3 .45 caliber holes, depending on how close your grouping is. The pasties are useful enough to extend each target by at least one more shooting group.

Here is a great suggestion to really extend the life of each target -- if you have guns of multiple calibers, start with your lowest caliber and work your way up. You can easily tell the difference between your .22 caliber hitsvs. your 9mm vs. your .45 caliber.

Using this methodology, you could probably use a single target up to 6 times, unless you are a nail driver and shoot out your bullseye really quickly!

The only downsides I can say are:

1) These targets are much more expensive than paper targets, but they're so easy to see that they're totally worth it for practicing your shooting and making adjustments after each shot.

2) The pasties can sometimes fly off when they get hit. Make sure you give them a good press and seal.
text_fidelity_b: Birchwood Casey Shoot-N-C, 8" Targets, Adhesive, See Hits Instantly

text_fidelity_a:
Proform Power 1080 Treadmill Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is a large treadmill with enough extra features to make workouts more enjoyable and more likely to take place. This treadmill is much more than a simple belt with readout of time and distance. Proform made this treadmill more sophisticated with multiple options, different workout plans, and added accessories to keep your workout running smoothly.

The Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is a high- tech machine and it has several different walking/jogging routines to suit your exercise needs. You can select what you want, tailored to your own needs, and perform your workout. The Proform Power 1080 Treadmill includes four main workout option categories: calorie burning workout, all- terrain, set a goal, and iFit, which uses wifi. No matter which option you use, the treadmill provides you with a full report showing your distance, average speed, elapsed time, vertical feet climbed, heart rate, and more.

Those who have not worked out much should probably begin with the set a goal workout or the calorie burning workout. The set a goal option lets you define a goal based on distance, time, or calorie- burning. The calorie- burning workout goes straight for the gut, letting you select a number of calories you would like to burn using pre- set options which can be adjusted to your own desired levels. These two are self- defined options make things easy through the use of defaulted settings, but you can still change them to suit your desires. For example, I may select a workout goal of 1 mile. The treadmill will default to a basic workout with inclines, varying speeds, etc. If I like, I can make a slight adjustment and, for example, change the time from 18 minutes to 12 and remove any percentage inclines. This is nice because the added flexibility lets you create a workout that is just right for you. Even after a workout has started, you can still make adjustments to the speed and percentage incline by pushing a button.

For the more advanced and/or more adventurous, this Proform treadmill has you covered. The iFit Live accesses more challenging workouts that are completely varied and the treadmill will change speed and incline on its own with greater frequency than you get with the calorie burning workout or other options. The idea is to make the experience similar to what you would go through if you were jogging through a place with varied hills, speeds, etc. It even accesses Google Maps to create a workout based on a specific location. The iFit feature requires accessing your wifi so it does take a little preparation, but the live action makes this one of the more enjoyable features of this treadmill. Once you setup an account, it remembers you and what you did the last time. It even keeps track of different family members and then reminds each of what they did before and what phase of the workout is next phase so that each person can pick up where they left off.

The Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is certainly a very cool, very modern treadmill, but is there anything that Proform overlooked or that needs improvement? Well, yes, there are a few things. One problem is the fan. The treadmill has a built- in fan and while this is certainly a good idea, the fan is far too weak to make it useful and there is no way to aim the air directly at your face. You need a second and better source of air than this to keep you cooled down and focused. Another surprising oversight is the lack of a holder for a water bottle. There are two square- shaped places where a beverage may be placed, but the shape isn't round and thus it will not hold a round bottle very securely. A third possible problem area for some is the time it takes for the screen to boot up. I find that the touch screen is responsive and works well, but it takes up to a minute after the power is turned on before the screen responds.

Exercising is certainly important and the Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is a very good, very sturdy treadmill with many features that work to encourage exercise. It isn't perfect, but with many cool and useful features like iFit, customized controls, sound systems for your iPod or MP3 player, and a solid warranty, this treadmill has much going for it and makes a very good choice for your next piece of exercise equipment.
text_fidelity_b: Proform Power 1080 Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Camp Creek 6-Person Tent (WARNING- This is an IN DEPTH review for those serious about making buying decisions. If you prefer a quick summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE
----------------
My family has been very enthusiastic about tent camping for quite some time. We have had a variety of tents over time, but one of our favorites was a Eureka one we had that was vintage. It was one of the last ones made in the US from what we understand and it lasted for a long time even past us getting it used. The design was perfect for the family and it was sturdy too. Had my husband not refused to stake it down one night insisting we would not get any wind, we would probably still have it. We got wind that night- so much that it pinned him against the building it blew him up against. He never refused again.

Our most recent tent experience has been horrible. We got a fantastic Coleman tent- great design- but the poles snapped the second time we used it- no wind, no bad weather- just snapped.

WHAT IS THIS TENT LIKE?
This tent is the most like the design of the Eureka we had some years ago that we have seen yet. I am going to break this down into sections about this tent so it is easier to work through to find what you want to know.

FABRIC
The fabric in this tent is as nice or nicer than the Colemans that we have had. It is gray, white, and teal. The screen is no-see-um netting but is thin- care needs to be taken to be sure it does not tear.

POLES
The poles are fantastic- best feature of this tent. The side poles are heavy steel with steel core shock cords in the poles. There are several shock corded fiberglass poles in this set. These poles go on top for a curved roof and also for the curved fly.

CONNECTORS
The connectors are all plastic, but quite sturdy- better than some of Coleman. Over time, I am not sure how they will hold up, but they are nice and sturdy.

STAKES
The stakes are about 8 inches long with a curved hook on top. They are about 1/4 inch thick straight rounded steel stakes- not something you will want to use in high winds or soil that is extremely wet or sandy. If you want something a little substantial or longer, you will have to purchase them. There are 13 stakes that come with this- for the tent and the cords that hold the tent stable.

WINDOWS
There is screen on the ceiling of the tent for a lot of circulation. It breathes nicely. The windows are also nice and large. However, one of my problems with this tent is that there are no ties for the windows to roll them up. They have to hang loose. I am not fond of that and wish they would have put ties or clips on them.

DOOR
There is a tie back for the door, but not the window in the door. The door is plenty roomy and opens nicely. It is not too far above the ground and opens with a nice zipper. If it were reinforced like some of the Coleman tents (with a little curved fiberglass pole around the edge and velcro to shut it as you go in and out) it would be perfect. Still it is pretty nice.

STAND UP ROOM
Everyone in the family has plenty of room to stand up straight including our 6 ft 3in member of the family.

SET UP
The set up of the tent is not difficult but it does take at least two people. If this is going to be put up in any kind of breeze, you will need three or four people to hold the tent from blowing away while you try to get it set up and staked down.

INSTRUCTIONS
The instructions are a nylon label sewn into the case. They are not particularly detailed when it comes to the extras like how to put the hanging storage in the tent. It is adequate for how to put up the tent, however, not a lot of detail beyond that.

CASE
Many times a tent comes in a very tiny case that does not store the tent once you have used it because the tent is often too big once it is rolled back up again. In this case, with some work, the case does fit the tent without too much struggle. It has a dual zipper. The tent comes with tiny ties in it that should be more substantial to help put the tent back.

FLY
The fly goes on well and does clip into place nicely.

WIND
Although this is difficult to put up in the wind (ask me how I know), once it is up and staked down with the lines and stakes and everything clipped as it should be, this tent is quite nice even in the wind. It stays pretty well although I would not expect it to make it through a very severe wind storm which most tents will not. For the usual weather, it seems to do fine.

WATERPROOF?
I did not have any experience with rain- the entire time the tent was set up, there was no rain. I will have to update about that.

PRIVACY
The top of this tent is white and quite thin. If you want privacy, you might want to keep in mind that you can probably see through it at night with a light on. The windows are a good height if you plan to sleep in a cot, mattress, or sleeping bag.

DURABILITY
Of course, I can only answer this over time, but so far, the construction of this tent is impressive, as long as you put down a tarp to protect the floor and keep applying waterproofing.

WEIGHT
This tent is made to stand up- that means that the poles are sturdy and strong. They are HEAVY. That means that this is a substantial package to carry. It is not for backpacking, but it will be a great base to set up if you are going out climbing or exploring with a small backpack tent.

WHAT I WISH THEY HAD DONE
I wish they had put ties on the windows. As small as that sounds, I think it matters in a tent situation. I also wish that they had a hook or ring coming down from the center of the ceiling to hang a lantern or light from.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite a few minor changes I would prefer, this is a nice tent. The poles are a great design and made to be strong. The package comes with everything you need to set up a sturdy nice tent, but you may want to purchase better stakes. A great comfortable tent for two to four people ( six if you are like sardines) if you keep up on treating for being waterproof, this tent could last some time if you take care of it. We love the design as a whole and are glad to have this.

MY RATING
Even though I would like a few different things with this- like tie backs on the windows, hook on the ceiling or even a reinforced door like Colemans have, None of these are enough to give it under five stars. The basic structure is great and hopefully will last longer than others on the market these days.

UPDATES
If you have a question about this tent that I have not addressed in this review, I will be happy to update if I can. Also, once we use it again next year I will update as well since we are approaching winter now.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Camp Creek 6-Person Tent

text_fidelity_a:
Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update) Picked up this tent after LOTS of searching and watching reviews. This tent is heavier than what I wanted for backpacking, however, I think the trade offs will be positive.
First off, the construction is very good out of the bag. All seams and tie out points are sealed with seam tape. No loose threads. The fly and tub are manufactured with a nice weight nylon, not too thin, and not too thick.
The newly designed corner sleeves for the poles are nice, this helps to pull the tent body nice and taut. Great design.
I like the color scheme as well, not too bright, but not drab either.
The aluminum pole segments seem to be shorter than most other tents, this should make it easy to pack in my back pack. I still have not decided if I will roll everything up in the storage bag and pack it vertically. Or use a stuff sack and shove the tent in the bottom of my pack and store the poles on the outside of the pack.
The vestibule is nice. It is not huge, but, it has plenty of room for shoes and some other items that you do not want to store in the tent. The ONE thing that sold me on this tent, is the way the vestibule zips open and closed. The last dome style I had with a vestibule, it zipped right down the middle. This made it hard to get to, as you had to basically crawl most of the way out of the tent to unzip it. This vestibule unzips right at the side of the entrance, which makes it super easy to open and close! AWESOME design!! More tent manufacturers need to use this design.
The only two cons I have right out of the packaging, is:
1. The tent IS on the heavy side, at almost 5 pounds. But, if you were backpacking with a friend or spouse, you could split up the pieces and make it lighter. But for a solo hiker, it is heavy. However, with the room you get, it is a good trade off.
2. The fly tie downs were just short loops of cordage that did not even reach the ground, and you cannot use the stakes to stake them out. Both sides and the rear are like this. I fixed this issue by just adding a length of cordage to all 3 spots.
I removed the supplied plastic line adjusters and just tied a taut line hitch on all pieces of cordage.
I will update after a few uses if need be.
text_fidelity_b: Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update)

It mounts "ok" but it's not as great as you would expect for a product that is made to work together. The clip mechanism is relatively easy to use to release the bike but it's fickle sometimes; often requiring quite a bit of effort to get clipped on or release. It feels like the clip mechanism does not move very freely and gets jammed with dirty easily. I strongly recommend getting the rain cover if you plan on using this in the rain without any other bags to put stuff in when the rain starts. I've been stuck in the rain a few times and the first time I didn't realize how porous the material of this bag was and my stuff got damp. Now, if I am expecting rain, I put my phone, hat and other things I want to keep dry in the waterproof pannier instead of the trunk bag.

Overall, this bag is great for light, dry weather commuter use. The removable shoulder strap is a nice touch. If you plan to ride in the rain either buy the rain cover, buy a different trunk or put your stuff in a waterproof bag.

text_fidelity_a:
UST TekFire Fuel-Free Lighter,orange If you want to get a fire going and you're using premade tinder or something homemade you're going to have to start small as the electrodes are rather close together. I was easily able to get small pieces of paper burning with little effort.
But to be honest? I burn a lot of Morning Star stick incense which fits perfectly between the electrodes of the TekFire. I got tired of grill/barbeque lighters with more safeties than some guns a few required two hands to operate or cheap lighters that even half full stop working after a few uses. I saw this rechargeable fuel-less lighter and have found i perfect for lighting my incense and tea lights as well as tall candles and oil lamps rather nicely. Durability is something we're going to have to see over time. The lighter comes with a two year warranty so there's plenty of time to give it a workout and see how it performs. So far? I'm very happy with this item.

Edit 10-06-2017 - This is sold as survival/camping gear. I simply use it around the house to light small candles and stick incense which small are a fairly tight fit between the electrodes. If this is meant for outdoor use why would they put a cheap, fragile and easily broken clear plastic hinge on the unit? Mine, after less than a month is severely wobbly. I would have no faith this would survive long term camping trips. I take care of my gear, as an example my backpack (a Jansport Eiger) is well over 30 years old. My sheath knife is similarly aged and even has my name and Explorer Post number scratched into the back of the sheath. I can't imagine this lighter lasting two years let alone 30+. I'm ready for the hinge to break any day now. I've dropped my review by one star due to poor quality/construction.
text_fidelity_b: UST TekFire Fuel-Free Lighter,orange

My daughter and I love hiking some of the local trails here in Oregon and I had ordered her a hydration pack a few months ago which has had some issues. The number one issue with hers is that she claims to this day that the water tastes weird. This particular Hydration Backpack has not had that issue, at least to me. Yes there was a bit of a taste in the beginning but after a few uses it is not as noticeable. I think this is probably an issue with any of these as the tubing and plastic bladder has a smell to begin with but eventually after some use and washing, it fades away. This Outdoor Revolution 16L Hydration Backpack is very well made. The bladder and tubing seems to be of a good quality. The backpack itself is well constructed with no loose or fraying of the stitching. It's quite comfortable to wear even when filled with water. There is even a bit of room for a few other things such as snacks, small first aid kit, mobile phone, charging cord etc. Overall I am impressed with this one and from what I can tell, it should hold up for a long time. I hope that this was helpful.

I've got a cow bell that got rung at 75 yards as many times as it got shot at - if that's not accurate for a red dot, I don't know what is. I was considering dripping a drop of epoxy on each corner (something I do with most of my $50 under reflex sights, but for this one I decided to leave it alone. After couple of times at the range, the glass gasket is still firmly in place - maybe I got a winner. I also like that they put a bit of thought in the design, as yes, it is silver, but the back housing (where the laser is) has a black top which minimizes glare - smart. So if someone had said - $20 and you got your self a keeper, I'd've said, ur kidding!

UPDATE:
Ooooooops... second outing. Didn't hold zero. Zero at holding zero (sorry, I had to). All of a sudden, I'm getting this jumps, vertically, horizontally. Try to adjust, then boom - it switches up 5 inches high at 50, boom you're now 3 inches to the left. Kept jumping all over the place. Right there and then, I put a zero on its life - it's at the bottom of a trash can. Look, if you LOVE wasting time and money, GET THIS! Otherwise, buy youself some good quality icecream for $20 - it'll be a MUCH better investment.
text_fidelity_b: HD101 4 Reticle Tactical Hunting Red/Green Dot Sight Tactical Reflex Rifle Scope with 20mm Rail

Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA This is an absolutely fantastic keeper glove with just one nuance with the right thumb fingersave.

The gloves are nice and cool with a mesh that lets the hand breathe on the back. The grip is great even though it is smooth! The palms are solid and feel like a mix of latex and neoprene and seem to breathe so my palms don't get as sweaty as other gloves. The latex is a bit soft and after a half-dozen practices with 4-5x the shots I would have in a game, it hasn't disappointed. However, there are some chunks that are missing. I change gloves nearly every season or two. There is a latex wraparound for the thumb that keeps the grip throughout the throw to my teammates. It's like I am getting an extra yard or two and can put a little spin on the ball if I like.

The hard ball comes in up high like a hornet and it's easy to swat down. I just don't feel the sting like some other, thinner, gloves have. Punching the ball is still possible with the fingersave *but* I rarely punch the ball.

The only thing I dislike is how they have the fingersave build into the thumb. It presses in on the top and side of the nail bed and is uncomfortable. I haven't found a way to push it down 1/2 inch and certainly can't change the angle. The left glove fits like, well, a glove and I barely notice the same thing but still notice it. Instead of a hard edge they might need to change the layout of the fingersave.

Normally I wear an Adidas or Reusch and this may be pushing Reusch out and into my new favorite. If I can figure a way out to warm up and melt the thumb fingersave to put a little curve into it, this would be the perfect glove.

I do not wash my gloves so haven't had any issues with the dye. I will gently wipe down the latex and the back of the glove unless the glove gets muddy. There are some renewal products that bring the tackiness back to the latex but I have not tried them with this glove.
text_fidelity_b: Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA

Magicmode Carbon Badminton Racket Set-with 6 Shuttlecocks and 1 Bag We have enjoyed playing badminton in a club setting, but due to Covid, have been unable to get back. So we decided to get a set for ourselves at home - as well as a net - and still be able to play. This set includes: a bag, 2 rackets, and container of 6 shuttlecocks. I would call this a set ideal for families, the backyard, beach, or picnics, but not for someone at the intermediate or advanced play/club play.

This is a great set. We got two nets here on Amazon for different settings, and took this set to our community tennis court.

The Bag: This is a great bag for this set. It allows one to carry both rackets and the tube of included shuttlecocks. That said, it would be a little better if the bag were even an inch longer. These are a tight fit at the current size. Even without the tube, these rackets have to be in essence pushed in in order to fit. But overall it's a great bag, looks great, and makes carrying easy.

The Rackets: These are nice. Again, this price point, these rackets are for family or couples looking for an hour of fun in the backyard, picnic, or on the beach - not a club setting. They have that nice sound when they connect, and they have a great distance on them. Lightweight, there was no fatigue after an hours play.

The Shuttlecocks: This is a great tube - 6 included. They are feathers, so nicer than the plastic kind. They get a nice sail to them. As feather, these will be damaged quickly, but one can continue to play for a good amount of time. We used one for a few games before needing to trade out. Plastic ones, once damaged, tend to need to be changed more quickly - in my experience.

This is a great set and for the right setting and players, perfect. We are happy and happy to recommend.

RockTape RockBand Flex Ultra-durable Resistance Bands with Handles and Loops I had some of the latex bands previously. It was very frustrating when they snapped in the middle of my exercising. This does not seem to have the same problem. Let's take a look at how they worked out for me..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This set is the light gray padded elastic set. That means that there is a light resistance. This is what I needed to help my body ease back into flexibility after having some physical problems to overcome. There is a book that has photos which show how to use the bands in a variety of different ways.

WHAT IS THE MANUAL LIKE?
First of all the manual has photos of each exercise with an explanation. It also has explanations of each set of exercises, what it does for the body and what the basics of these systems in the body are like and how they work. The manual is easy to understand and does outline all of the exercises well. I do appreciate the explanations. I also appreciate the rock tape on some of the models so that it shows how to use that as well.

HOW WAS THIS TO WORK WITH?
Some of the exercises in this manual require that you have a place to attach the band securely to do them. That means you have to have a loop, hook, or other place to anchor the band to do some of the exercises. If you don't that eliminates a lot of the exercises. I found that this did help me to rehabilitate my body slowly and gradually without the fear of the bands snapping.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice non-breaking way of using bands for rehabilitation or gradual strength building. The manual helps to outline how to use the bands and give ideas how the body works and how the bands help.

MY RATING
Four stars for this. I would like the bands to be a little wider and more substantial than they are- they are a bit narrow. However, it does work well and I am glad to have used this set.
text_fidelity_b: RockTape RockBand Flex Ultra-durable Resistance Bands with Handles and Loops

text_fidelity_a:
BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids. I purchased this to use on my bicycle that I use for commuting. I leave early in the morning while it is still dark. The route I take is pretty well lit with street lights so I use the lights mostly for visibility and not to light the road in front of me.

The mounts are pretty simple to use. I attached the front to the handlebar and the back to the basket I have on the rear rack. The front light has 3 steady settings at 3 levels of brightness and one flashing mode. I am not sure how useful the level of brightness would be in absolute darkness as far as seeing the path in front of you because I have not used it in that scenario, but it seems pretty bright to me. I keep it on flashing mode for visibility. It is conveniently re-chargeable via USB cord and it seems to last adequately between charges.

I gave this product a 3 star rating because the back light does not work the way I need it to. The first time I used it, I thought I turned it on but when I got to my destination it was off so I figured I forgot to turn it on. The second time I used it on the return trip, I made absolutely sure it was on when I started and when I got to the destination it was off again. I took the light off my bike and turned it on and dropped it onto a hard surface from a distance of less than 3 inches and it shut off. Since this is battery operated and not rechargeable, I'm guessing the batteries get jolted from going over a bump on the road and shuts off on its own. It lights up again without any issues if you press the on button again, but that is not feasible or safe to reach behind you and fix it if you are riding on a road with vehicular traffic all around you. It is also very inconvenient to pull over to the side every time it shuts off to turn it back on again. Since the light set was fairly inexpensive, I just purchased a different separate backlight from the local box store to replace it.

I will not go through the time and inconvenience of returning the item or exchanging it because it simply is not worth it. I hope the seller doesn't try to contact me to "fix" the problem because they will be wasting their time.
text_fidelity_b: BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids.

I like to use them with smaller tents on the windward side of the tent, to give a little better holding power than the shorter stakes offer, and on the sheltered side of larger tents, where you don't need such a strong hold (with longer stakes on the windward side). VENZO Compatible with Shimano SPD Mountain Bike CNC Cr-Mo Die-Cast Aluminum Sealed Pedals with Cleats - Dual Platform Clipless Pedals for Mountain Bike Shoes - Easy Clip in & Out I'm not really much of a bike rider, but lately I've been going on some longer trips (about 20 miles once a week or so) and decided that it might be worth my while to invest in some clip in pedals. After reading about the two main types of clipless systems, I decided the SPD-style pedals would better fit my bill and budget, and desire to stay around $100 together with shoes. Installation was a breeze, once I purchased an additional wrench to get my unexpectedly heavy old regular rectangle pedals off, and these Venzo brand pedals slipped right into place.

I haven't had any issues with the tension of the clipping mechanism after three solid rides so far, though I did have a bolt fall out of my shoe causing the shoe to get stuck clipped into the pedal -- I releasing the tension all the way got the shoe out but the small metal piece which the tension screw screws into is rather difficult to get back into position if it happens to fall out.

The included cleats fit nicely on the shoes I bought and other than some embarrassing falls and general awkwardness getting in/out of the pedals, I haven't had any issues with these pedals. If you are a beginning cyclist like myself looking for an affordable entry to clipless pedal systems, these fit the bill well. I also have taken some shorter trips with regular non clip-in shoes with these and they are acceptably fine.

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black

AKUSAKO Camping Propane Heater - 2 In 1 Outdoor Portable Gas Heater & Stove Included Tent Heaters + Propane Hose Kit for Regulator Applicable For Ice Fishing Backpacking Hiking Hunting(Orange) Actually, I think this is a good buy. It has a piezo ignition that works. It puts out plenty of heat. Although I don't envision cooking on it I can see where it would handle the task ok but I would be worried about boilovers putting out the flame. This thing puts out a ton of heat and is sufficiently adjustable in output.

Pros. It easily lights. Puts out sufficient heat and does so at 360 degrees all around. It is larger than expected which I think is a good thing. The base seems stable. The output is adjustable.

Cons. The biggest fault I find is the warning on the outside of the heater which states "For Outdoor Use Only" when in fact the Title or Heading states, "AKUSAKO Camping Propane Heater - 2 In 1 Outdoor Portable Gas Heater & Stove Included Tent Heaters " Note it says "tent heater." So, now I am not so sure. It would likely be fine but I would not operate it indoors without a CO and Oxygen monitor, which I own anyway. It is not a good idea to operate any propane device in a tent without the monitors anyway.

The rubber feet (3) are all stripped out. The rubber feet screw through a fairly thin metal plate that was stripped out at the factory. Note that this can probably be easily remedied by using a slightly larger sheet metal screw instead of what appears to be a small wood screw, just don't overtighten.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included) I'm a long-time Fitbit user. I started out with my all-time favorite, the One, which was totally accurate and counted stairs. I replaced it with a Zip, which was also totally accurate but didn't count stairs, and mine went through batteries fast. I owned a couple Altas, that weren't accurate at all and I hated the charging cable.

And that brings me to the Inspire, which I'm pretty happy with. I'm going to start with the things I like about it.

I like the face options and how easy they are to change, the touchscreen - once you get used to it, it's very informative and easy to use, and I like the build quality, which is much nicer than the Zip for the same price I paid for the Zip a few years ago. I guess I got lucky - the unit uses about 10% of the battery per day. I very much prefer the way the Inspire docks in its charging cable - such an improvement over the Alta clips cable! And I've always had good luck getting support from Fitbit - when I had questions about the Inspire, I used their live chat and the rep was helpful and took her time.

Now for a neutral. My Inspire is reasonably accurate but not dead on. If I take 50 steps, it'll count 54 or 47. I can live with that. My One and Zip spoiled me, but both Altas were WAY off, which made me stop using a Fitbit for a while - no sense in wearing one if the counts are off by 25% to 30% (which they were).

There are cons. My first one only applies if you're a long-time Fitbit user and are used to using the wireless dongle so your Fitbit can communite with your computer. You won't be able to use the dongle because the Inspire uses Bluetooth rather than wireless to connect. I liked syncing with my computer, but opted to just sync with my phone as you now have to create a Microsoft account in order to download Fitbit Connect.

I found the band impossible to put on, but I mostly wear it on a clip, and there are some much easier to close and more attractive third-party bands for it on Amazon. It didn't recognize me cycling, and while that didn't bother me, it's worth noting - it would have been cool if that feature had worked.

My Inspire has made me a happy camper. I like wearing a Fitbit, seeing my steps and active minutes - that's why I've owned them. I find the Fitbit dashboard info and the quick stats on the screen motivating, and while I loved my One, the display on the Inspire gives more info more easily thanks to the touchscreen. I like the menus on the Inspire itself, the touchscreen and the charger. Oh, and I think the price ($58 when I bought it) is quite reasonable and a good value. I'm glad I got it :)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included)

Pinci Rechargeable Hand Warmers, Reusable Electric Heater, 5000mAh Portable USB-C PowerBank, 360° Heat 3 Levels Pocket Warmers for Raynauds Outdoor Camping Gifts for Men Women Kids(Green) I really wanted to like this item. I really did. I thought it was going to be ideal - a hand warmer for those cold times, with the addition of it being a spare portable 5K power bank. Sadly, it does neither of them very well.

I charged this item for several hours after receiving - there are not indicators that let you know when it is fully charged or still needing to be charged. I tried it as a hand warmer first.

The controls are very problematic - the enclosed instruction leaflet has text so small that it is impossible to read, even with a magnifying glass. The instructions on the Amazon Product Description page do not seem to accurately match this product, and attempting the required button presses/pauses do not seem to lead to a function you want. I kept turning the useless LED lights on when what I wanted was the warmer function.

When I was finally able to turn on the hand warmer function, I was very disappointed. There are 3 settings, which seem to be low, lower and very very low. The Amazon Product Description page indicates the highest setting should be 50 C - 55 C. This converts to 122 F - 131 F. This should be hot - very very hot. Instead, at the highest setting (called 3rd gear, curiously) the hand warmer is barely warm, not enough to even warm your hand effectively. The first 2 settings are even lower, and as equally useless.

I did not really need this as a power bank, but felt the need to test that function also. Besides the fact that there is no way to tell how much power is left in this device, or if it is charging or needs charging, it is very very slow to recharge my phone. I used a a 60W charging cable, and it took several hours to charge my phone from 47% to 95%. I gave up after that, frustrated at its slowness.

This device works poorly at either of its listed functions. Perhaps as a paperweight, but I don't think it would work well at that either. I unfortunately cannot recommend this product.
text_fidelity_b: Pinci Rechargeable Hand Warmers, Reusable Electric Heater, 5000mAh Portable USB-C PowerBank, 360° Heat 3 Levels Pocket Warmers for Raynauds Outdoor Camping Gifts for Men Women Kids(Green)

I just took it out of the box, and it made a tearing/popping noise while feeling it up for integrity; if the sound was micro tears in the aluminum, that's pretty much exposing the user to a lot more aluminum than expected, and defeating the main purpose of anodized aluminum, that is to have a thicker outer layer of non-reactive oxidized aluminum. There are scratches around the rim where the lid rests, which is absolutely unacceptable for a brand new product.

The tea kettle has a chalkboard like feel to touch, in a bad way, and it left a sticky residue on my finders after handling it. The bottom was bent slightly; enough to pop in and out when pressed gently, leading me to believe it was previously used, defective, or just a bad product. I've used cheapo, don't-care-if-get-stepped-on pots that were more sturdy than this one, granted they didn't look as nice.

It was smaller than I expected, but just fine for boiling water, which is seemed to do in a typical amount of time for any pot with the same amount of water. If it had cost $5 I would keep it, because it is convenient and you can boil water in it. Heck, I'd probably pay $10 for it because it looks great, but for $25 the quality is atrocious.

text_fidelity_a:
Eureka! Solitaire AL 1 Person, 3 Season, Camping and Backpacking Tent This Eureka Solitaire should be considered more as a bivy than a tent. I suppose it is more a bivy/tent hybrid. Being an inbetween, it is not super light, but is not super heavy either. Weight on this is 3 lbs, 2 oz. That is with poles, stakes, guy lines, and carry bag. So the tent is not an ultralight, especially for the size of this thing.
Pros:
1. Packs down small and does not take up much room in a backpack.
2. Fairly light
3. Fly can be rolled up to allow for maximum airflow when the weather permits.
Cons:
1. Not free standing. Must be staked down.
2. Fly is not removable.
3. No vestibule.
4. Must crawl in/out from the front. Can be hard to keep from getting wet/dirty if there was a storm/rain the night before.

Overall, if you are looking for a bivy style tent, this probably is what you want. Unless you want an ultra-light, which this is not.
I personally would not recommend this style of tent. But, if you are looking for a nicely built bivy tent, this is probably it, if you do not mind the weight.
Would be really good for motorcycle or bike camping. Not really for backpacking, as the weight is comparable to a good 2 person tent!
If I were going to carry a 3lb+ tent, I would get one with enough room to sit up in and that has a vestibule. Plenty of those tents out there in the 3lb range.
text_fidelity_b: Eureka! Solitaire AL 1 Person, 3 Season, Camping and Backpacking Tent

This vest is a great option for our little girl who is so very close to swimming on her own but is not quite safe in deep water yet without a floatie. The puddle-jumper style floaties are great and have worked well for her, but she has more flexibility in this vest and can practice swimming strokes quite easily in this.

It’s easy to get on and take off, with a nice size zipper. The zipper pull could possibly be a little larger for little hands, but it’s quite practical as is. And the Velcro tab that covers the zipper pull is a nice touch.

The strap between the legs is purposeful in making sure that the vest doesn’t rise too far up from the body, but it has been a little annoying to my girl. The wide pad that covers the strap is good in theory but has seemed bulky between her legs.

Our daughter doesn’t need the chin float element, so it’s nice that the chin float is so easy to unsnap and then re-snap on if necessary.

Also, the vest has a good bit of flexibility. The floatation elements within the fabric of the vest are layered, thin floatation pads (two in the back and four in the front). This layering of thin pads provides for a soft, flexible fit.

All in all, this is a great floatation vest for our emerging little swimmer.

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Flash Belt 17oz I wanted to like this belt because it is simple and lightweight, but it is expensive for what you get and I think there are a couple of important problems with the design. First, the main purpose of a hydration belt is to hold your water. This belt comes with an insulated water bottle, but the bottle is a non-standard size so you have to use their bottle. The bottle is narrower at the bottom than at the top, which helps you push it into its pocket. Unfortunately, no other bottles that I tried (including Camelbak bicycle water bottles) will fit (either the bottles are too wide or they fall out too easily).

Another problem is the single zippered pocket. The pocket will hold a phone up to about 6 inches tall. However, there is also a key ring in this pocket and I don't want my keys banging against my phone. I wish there was a smaller zippered pocket away from the phone pocket for keys. There is an open pocket on the other side that I assume if for holding energy gels.

The water bottle holds 17 ounces of water, which isn't that much, but that is usually plenty for me on a 1 hour run. Camelbak makes much larger hydration packs for hikers or mountain bikers that work well, but I am glad that have a lightweight option for joggers and runners. I just wish it was a little more functional and more competitively priced. There are lots of other runner hydration belts on the market.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Flash Belt 17oz

Frankford Arsenal Quick-N-EZ 110V Case Tumbler Kit with Sifter for Brass Cartridge Cleaning and Polishing for Reloading [[VIDEOID:4d97ce6c49de579dc9b8d7678abf3b9f]] Maybe it is a little early for this review since I got this yesterday but I am very impressed and this has been run about 16 hours out of the last 20. I set it on a smart plug timer so it could even do a late night batch without running all night. I used to do ultrasonic cleaning but I hated the drying process and the less pleasing lack of that brassy shine you get with tumbling.
A couple pieces of advice....I saw reviewers mentioning the center bolt dinging up brass, the fix is SUPER easy. A simple drinking straw to cover the threads. I even found a blue one that matches the tumbler.
Second piece of advice, don't be dumb like me. I had a handful of .223 that I decided to add to the .40 cal I was tumbling. .223 fits in the .40 cal so many of the .223 had unpolished bases. Just remember 9 mm fits in .40 and .40 fits in .45. so pay attention if you mix brass. Make sure it can't fit inside the other type.
